title: Slow order submissions behind incomplete traces

sources.claim: Incoming requests to Cloud Run services automatically generate traces without instrumentation; traceparent is automatically populated for Cloud Run requests; Cloud Run samples at most 0.1 requests per second per instance and its sample rate is not configurable; instrumentation is needed for custom spans and to propagate trace context so a multi-service request shows as one trace. The page does not name the automatic span or list its attributes, so the fixture's span wording is not graded.

traceparent carries trace ID, parent span ID and the sampling flag; X-Cloud-Trace-Context carries TRACE_ID/SPAN_ID;o=OPTIONS; Cloud Trace is not responsible for context propagation, and without a suitable instrumentation library the application must propagate context to child operations. The page does not describe how a dropped header is displayed.
A receiver that gets no traceparent header creates a new trace-id and parent-id for the current request, which is why an unpropagated downstream call appears as a separate root trace.

Propagators inject context into a carrier such as HTTP headers on the sender and extract it on the receiver; the default propagator uses W3C TraceContext; propagation is usually handled by instrumentation libraries, so an uninstrumented client does not propagate it automatically.

The LogEntry trace field links logs and traces (the REST resource-name form is supported); httpRequest.latency is server processing time from request receipt until the response is sent, so it does not separate platform from in-container time.

Cloud Run creates request logs automatically under the cloud_run_revision resource with project_id, location, service_name and revision_name labels; container logs are not correlated to request traces unless written with a client library or a logging.googleapis.com/trace field.

a.conclusion: Each slow trace, and the baseline, holds only the span Cloud Run recorded for the incoming request; its duration matches the roughly 4 s logged server latency. order-router exports no application spans, so the traces confirm server-side delay from receipt to response but cannot split it between platform handling, in-process work, positions-db, pricing-engine or Pub/Sub. The missing child spans are an instrumentation gap, not evidence that no dependency work happened or that Cloud Run added the latency.

The order-router trace is incomplete, not the whole request; the delay most probably lies in the pricing-engine call, paired by timing rather than shared context, and its internal cause is unknown.
